test_title: PYST 56: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held on 05 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: english
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses **elements that influence or decide** why behaviour happens, which aligns with the definition of '**determinants**.'
 
• **Determinants of behaviour** are **factors or elements** that contribute to the manifestation of certain actions or patterns of actions. This fits the context of discussing motivation as an underlying factor.
 
• Using 'determinants' underscores the idea that motivations are not just incidental but play a crucial role in shaping behaviour across different scenarios.

Therefore, the correct answer is- "determinants".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Option 1 (**meaning**): Refers to the significance or interpretation of something, which is not the focus here.
 
• Option 2 (**causes**): Imply direct factors leading to an effect, but 'determinants' offer a broader understanding of influences on behaviour.
 
• Option 3 (**ways**): Suggests methods or approaches, not the underlying reasons or factors that motivate behaviour.

Complete passage is__: The concept of motivation focuses on explaining what ‘moves’ behaviour. In fact, the term (1)motivation is derived from the Latin word ‘movere’, referring to movement of activity. Most of our everyday explanation of (2)behaviour is given in terms of motives. Motives also help in making (3)predictions about behaviour. A person will work hard in school, in sports, in business, in music, and in many other situations, if he/she has a very strong need for (4)achievements. Hence, motives are the general states that enable us to make predictions about behaviour in many different situations. In other words, motivation is one of the (5)determinants of behaviour. Instincts, drives, needs, goals, and incentives come under the broad cluster of motivation.
